x: One Dobson Unit is a layer of pure ozone 0.01 mm thick at 0°C and 1 atmosphere. The traps change the thickness or the temperature.
t: Recall the definition of the Dobson Unit.

x: Option C is incorrect: the Kigali Amendment, which phases down HFCs, came into force on 1 January 2019, not 2020.
t: Recall the Kigali start date.

x: Both are true: stratospheric ozone protects life because it absorbs harmful ultraviolet rays. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the absorption explains the protection.

x: UV-A is 315–400 nm, UV-B 280–315 nm, and UV-C 100–280 nm, the shortest and most harmful. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-i.
t: Remember: wavelength falls from A to C.

x: All four are correct: the Montreal Protocol and Vienna Convention protect the ozone layer, a British team found the Antarctic ozone hole (1985), and G.W. Kent Moore described the Tibetan ozone low.
t: Recall the ozone facts.

x: All four are correct: ozone is O₃, three oxygen atoms, found mainly in the stratosphere, and formed when UV splits O₂.
t: Recall how ozone forms.

x: Both are true: about 90% of ozone is in the stratosphere and about 10% in the troposphere.
t: Recall the 90:10 split.

x: Both are true: ground-level (tropospheric) ozone is a pollutant because it harms living things. R explains A.
t: Discriminate good ozone from bad ozone.

x: All six deplete ozone: CFCs, halons, carbon tetrachloride, HCFCs, methyl chloroform and methyl bromide.
t: Recall the ozone-depleting substances.

x: The stratosphere spans about 10–50 km, and the main ozone layer lies within it at about 15–30 km. The traps swap the two ranges.
t: Remember the ozone layer lies inside the stratosphere.

x: World Ozone Day is 16 September, also called the International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer; the UN declared it in 1994, and it marks the signing of the Montreal Protocol. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Match each item to its detail.

x: Both are true: ozone loss is linked with CFCs and other ODS, and CFCs are used as refrigerants. Their use does not explain how they harm ozone, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a use explains an effect.

x: The World Heritage Convention (UNESCO, 1972) protects cultural and natural heritage. Ramsar covers wetlands and the CBD biodiversity.
t: Match each treaty to its subject.

x: Option C is incorrect: the Rotterdam Convention covers prior informed consent for hazardous chemicals and pesticides. Biosafety and GMOs come under the Cartagena Protocol.
t: Discriminate Rotterdam from Cartagena.

x: Both are true: the Montreal Protocol controls the making and use of ozone-depleting substances because those substances are what it was made to deal with. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the subject explains the controls.

x: The CBD covers biodiversity conservation, Cartagena biosafety and GMOs, Nagoya access and benefit sharing, and ITPGRFA plant genetic resources for food. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Match each treaty to its subject.

x: All three are correct: the UNFCCC (1992) is the climate framework, Kyoto (1997) set emission commitments, and Paris (2015) set the temperature goal.
t: Arrange the climate treaties in time order.

x: Ramsar dates from 1971, the World Heritage Convention 1972, the CBD 1992, and the Cartagena Protocol 2000. The answer is a-i, b-iv, c-ii, d-iii.
t: Arrange the treaties in time order.

x: I and II are correct: the Nagoya Protocol was adopted in 2010, and the plant treaty (ITPGRFA) in 2001. III is false because it gives the wrong year for the plant treaty.
t: Discriminate 2001 from 2010.

x: Two are correct: the Montreal Protocol came into force on 1 January 1989, and Ozone Day is 16 September. III is false because 16 September is the signing anniversary, not the start date.
t: Discriminate the signing date from the start date.

x: Both are true: the UNCCD deals with desertification, and UNCLOS with the oceans and the law of the sea.
t: Expand each short name.

x: The Montreal Protocol was signed on 16 September 1987 and came into force on 1 January 1989.
t: Discriminate the signing year from the start year.
